question: In 1889, ________ established the Mukti Mission, in Pune, a refuge for young widows who had been deserted and abused by their families.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandita Ramabai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pandita Ramabai** was a renowned social reformer and educationist in India, particularly known for her efforts in women's emancipation.
 
• She established the **Mukti Mission** in 1889 in Pune, Maharashtra, as a refuge for young widows who faced desertion and abuse.
 
• The Mukti Mission provided widows with shelter, education, and vocational training, aiming to help them achieve self-reliance.
 
• Ramabai was a pioneer in advocating for the rights of women, especially widows, during a time when they faced severe social stigma and hardships.
 
• She was also an accomplished scholar of Sanskrit and a key figure in the 19th-century Indian social reform movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Widowhood in 19th-Century India:**

 
 
• Widows during this period were often ostracized, deprived of property rights, and subjected to severe societal discrimination.
 
• Social reformers like Pandita Ramabai sought to challenge these oppressive customs and provide avenues for widows to rebuild their lives.
 
 
 
• **Mukti Mission:**
 
 
• Initially started as a shelter for young widows, it later expanded into a broader initiative for women's empowerment.
 
• The Mission provided education, healthcare, and skill development, fostering independence among its residents.
 
 
 
• **Pandita Ramabai’s Legacy:**
 
 
• She was honored with the title "Pandita" due to her profound knowledge of Sanskrit and religious texts.
 
• Her autobiography, *My Testimony*, and other writings highlighted the plight of Indian women and advocated social reform.
 
 
 
• **Other Social Reformers of the Era:**
 
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy and Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar were among her contemporaries who worked to abolish harmful practices like Sati and child marriage.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj, Arya Samaj, and similar movements played a key role in shaping 19th-century social reforms.
